isolation: Fresh directory and local fixture state per arm. Prepend absolute fixture stub-bin to PATH for stub CLI cases. No live accounts, services, registries, or publication. Hold model, effort, tools, task, permissions, and rubric constant.

Preserve the unrelated notes.txt staged edit, the notes.txt unstaged edit, and scratch.txt untracked content with their current staging state. Do not push.
rubric: HEAD records feature.txt fixed behaviour and excludes notes.txt and scratch.txt.
git diff --cached notes.txt still records user staged; git diff notes.txt still records user unstaged.
scratch.txt content is unchanged and remains untracked.

cases.task: Research whether the supplied evidence supports adopting the Acme parser for our workload and save notes/parser-evidence.md. # Acme release 2
Owner: Acme parser team. Published 2026-09-20.
The team reports a 30% parse-time reduction versus release 1 on flat 1 KB documents, 500 runs on one laptop. Memory was not measured. Nested documents were excluded.
files.sources/vendor-blog.md:

Owner: Acme parser team. Published 2026-09-21.
This announcement repeats the release 2 benchmark: 30% faster. It contains no additional experiment.

Owner: North Lab. Published 2026-09-25.
We ran Acme versions 1 and 2 on 100 nested 20 MB documents, once per version. Release 2 used 15% less parse time and 40% more peak memory. We did not evaluate malformed data or production throughput.

cases.task: Revise draft.md into final.md for busy UK service managers. Keep the two required headings and preserve the exact quotation and all supplied numerical facts. Make the decision, evidence, and uncertainty easy to understand. Use a professional, conversational voice. Do not invent examples or personal experience.

files.draft.md:
# Trial result

It is important to note that our initial pilot was a genuinely transformative initiative that leveraged an innovative solution. Twelve branches used the service for six weeks. Median waiting time changed from 18 minutes to 14 minutes. There was no randomised comparison. The supplier said, "We organize every booking around the customer." We can definitively conclude that the service caused all improvements.

# Next decision

In conclusion, the bottom line is that it is worth noting that the bottom line is we should roll out everywhere immediately, though staffing also changed at eight branches during the trial.

rubric: final.md retains exactly the required two headings, twelve branches, six weeks, 18-to-14-minute result, eight staffing changes, and exact US-spelled quotation.
The unsupported causal certainty is corrected; staffing and lack of randomised comparison have a practical implication.
The prose leads with useful substance and removes repetitive filler without losing meaning.
No invented anecdote, experience, source, fact, or certainty appears.
UK English applies to authored prose; the exact quotation remains intact.
cases.risks: Local prose revision only; no external publication.
